hero.lead: A nation of 5.3 million whose power is four fifths renewable and whose Treasury cut its 2026/27 bond programme by NZ$4 billion to NZ$30 billion in September 2026 as the budget improved.

capital.heading: A clean grid and a shrinking borrowing programme.

record.text: Government bond programme for 2026/27 after the pre-election update, down NZ$4 billion from the Budget
Gross bond issuance planned for the four years to June 2030 at Budget 2026, down from NZ$130 billion
Net core Crown debt at 30 September 2026, 42.3% of GDP, close to the forecast of the pre-election update

register.name: Government bond programme, 2026/27
register.detail: New Zealand Debt Management · Budget 2026, 28 May 2026 · reduced by NZ$4bn at the Pre-election Economic and Fiscal Update, 29 September 2026
register.note: The Treasury reduced the bond programme by NZ$4 billion in 2026/27 and by NZ$15 billion over the whole forecast period, against Budget 2026
register.text: Nominal and inflation-indexed New Zealand Government Bonds planned for 2026/27, including a new May 2038 line. They finance the Crown’s budget, which carries the public services behind the seven standards.

register.name: New Zealand Sovereign Green Bond Programme
register.detail: New Zealand Debt Management · NZ$9.93bn on issue at 30 June 2025 · NZ$3.33bn issued in 2024/25, fully allocated · NZ$9,720.3M allocated in 2021–2025 · Allocation and Impact Report 2025
register.note: Green social housing took NZ$809.6 million of the 2025 allocation and NZ$2,109.5 million in 2021–2025; 1,085 households accommodated in 2025
register.text: Green bonds of the New Zealand Government whose net proceeds are allocated to eligible public spending on clean transport, green buildings, climate change adaptation, biodiversity, energy efficiency and renewable energy, and water and wastewater. Green social housing within the green buildings category serves the shelter standard; the energy and water spending serves the energy and water standards.

register.name: Community Housing Provider Loan Guarantee Scheme
register.detail: Minister of Finance and Minister of Housing · announced 1 October 2025 · Crown guarantee of 80% of eligible loans · up to NZ$80M per provider · ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Kiwibank and Westpac · loans available until 30 June 2027
register.note: The amount is the new lending and refinancing the scheme can support, not the guarantee itself
register.text: A Crown guarantee of 80 per cent of the loans that five participating banks make to eligible community housing providers, which lowers their cost of borrowing. The Government is working with community housing providers on more than 2,000 new social homes, so the scheme serves the shelter standard.

register.name: Green, Social and Sustainability loans to councils
register.detail: New Zealand Local Government Funding Agency · seven loans approved by June 2025 · NZ$453.9M advanced · Annual Impact Report 2025, 30 September 2025 · Sustainable Financing Bonds of NZ$2.26bn due 2030 and NZ$1bn due 2032
register.note: Includes up to NZ$55 million borrowed by Christchurch City Council to finance Ōtautahi Community Housing Trust, which had built 312 of 366 homes by 30 June 2025
register.text: Loans from the Local Government Funding Agency, owned 80% by 30 councils and 20% by the New Zealand Government, for council projects that meet green, social or sustainability criteria: green buildings, climate change adaptation, biodiversity and affordable housing. The affordable housing loan serves the shelter standard, and flood protection such as RiverLink in the Hutt Valley protects homes.
by: New Zealand Local Government Funding Agency

register.name: Crown lending facilities to the Community Housing Funding Agency
register.detail: Cabinet agreed 24 March 2025 · NZ$100M provided by the Minister of Finance in April 2025 · up to NZ$50M more once the credit rating was well advanced, NZ$30M held as a contingency · final repayment by 30 June 2029
register.note: Papers released by the Treasury in November 2026; the Agency had 10 community housing provider borrowers in June 2025
register.text: Commercially priced, revolving Crown lending to the Community Housing Funding Agency, drawn as it lends to community housing providers and repaid from bonds sold to wholesale investors. It widens the providers’ access to debt finance for social homes and serves the shelter standard.

register.name: Debut social bonds, three and five years
register.detail: Community Housing Funding Agency · NZ$100M of 3-year and NZ$100M of 5-year social bonds · issuer rating A+ from S&P Global · ANZ sole arranger and lead manager · announced 29 September 2025
register.note: RNZ reports that the Agency was launched in 2024 by the social enterprise Community Finance
register.text: The first social bonds of the Community Housing Funding Agency, which aggregates the borrowing requirements of community housing providers and issues high-grade debt securities to wholesale investors. The proceeds fund lending to providers that build and run social homes, serving the shelter standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Four fifths of the power from water, geothermal heat and wind.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Pasture and orchards across more than a third of the land: dairy, meat and fruit for the world.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Native bush and planted forest across two fifths of the land.

items.name: The Visitors
items.label: Of export earnings from visitors, 2018
items.text: Mountains, fiords and Māori culture: visitors earned almost a fifth of exports.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 17.9% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Everybody Eats
items.text: A food rescue charity, established in 2017, that serves restaurant-quality meals made from rescued food in three restaurants, two in Auckland and one in Wellington, on a pay-what-you-can system in which diners pay it forward so that others can eat out whatever their circumstances.

items.name: Community Finance
items.text: A social enterprise that finances community housing and in 2024 launched the Community Housing Funding Agency, which won an A+ credit rating from S&P Global in September 2025 to issue social bonds that fund community housing providers at lower interest rates.

items.name: Tū Mai Rā Energy
items.text: An energy business owned and operated by Rangitāne iwi that installs solar panels and batteries on marae: five marae from Whanganui to Taumarunui ran on solar in May 2026, eight were due by the end of June, and 32 had registered their interest.

items.name: Dignity
items.text: A period equity business that supplies organic cotton period products to workplaces on a buy one, give one basis and donates the same number to community organisations: more than 1.4 million products donated with 140 corporate partners, and free products for nearly 1,000 women apprentices through BCITO from November 2025.

items.name: will&able
items.text: A social enterprise that employs more than 120 neurodivergent and differently abled New Zealanders in assembling, cleaning, packaging and sorting work and in its own product range, creating more than 2,600 hours of paid work every week.
